newsitem.title: SENEGAL: Senegal Telecoms union says privatisation too slow.
newsitem.headline: Senegal Telecoms union says privatisation too slow.

text.p: The workers union at Senegal's telecommunications company Sonatel said on Monday it was concerned at delays in completing privatisation of the state firm.
Senegal last year struck a provisional deal to sell a strategic one-third stake in Sonatel to Swedish-led consortium Telia Overseas last December.

"We are in March 1997 and the signing and sealing of the final choice of the consortium led by Telia has not taken place yet and the new company is still waiting to start off," the Sonatel Workers Union said in a statement.
"Delays (in privatisation) from one week to another are heavily prejudicial to Sonatel," it added.
Communication Minister Serigne Diop told reporters last Thursday the government was set to finalise the agreement signed with Telia last November.
"We have almost finished. A final signing of the accord with the consortium will take place soon," he said last week.
Under the provisional deal, the consortium would pay up to 70 billion CFA francs ($121 million), representing one third of the projected capital of Sonatel.
Other members of the consortium include the Walter Group of the United States, China Telecommunication Services and private Senegalese company Senecom Partners.
The remaning shares were to be sold to private Senegalese and African investors with 10 percent reserved for Sonatel staff.
Senegal has also announced it will liberalise its cellular telephone sector next year, with January as the target date for the start of a second network.
Sonatel (Societe Nationale des Telecomunication du Senegal) started the West African nation's first cellular telephone service in October, using a GSM system and now has some 2,500 subscribers.
Sonatel has a capital of 50 billion CFA francs and an annual turnover of more than 60 billion CFA francs.
